transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes (recording stopped at 10:48)
Location: Zoom / Internal
Notes: internal retrospective on operational runway and fast-fail cadence; mix of product/infra/ops
Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Leah, Carlos, Ari, Samir, Elena, Rina

Summary (auto):
Quick retrospective on recent fast-fail experiments during the December rollout window. Focus on what failed/what succeeded, instrumentation gaps, and an agreement on a short checklist for future fast-fail attempts plus canary schedule and owners. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Fast-fail experiments and outcomes
- Instrumentation and observability gaps
- Canary/runbook updates
- Rollback criteria and SLA communication
- Postmortem friction and followups

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: Okay, everyone, thanks for doing this in the window before holidays. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:10] Samir: Yeah, good.
[00:12] Jonah: yep, good here.
[00:18] Maya: Great. So objective for today is a tight retro on the fast-fail approach we used on the dec launch, make fixes to the runbook and assign owners. I want us to be able to run a proper canary in January. 45 minutes on ops, 20 product decisions, then wrap.
[00:34] Elena: Sounds good. I put a quick slide in the chat with a timeline and the big incidents.
[00:40] Maya: Cool — link looks like: drive.redwood/runbooks/fast-fail-dec2026 (note: placeholder), thanks.
[00:48] Rina: Real quick summary — two fast-fail experiments: model B quantization toggle, and a prefix-cache eviction test. Quantization experiment dropped P95 by ~18% but raised hallucination regressions on one eval set. Cache eviction lowered cost but increased tail latency on certain routes.
[01:10] Carlos: Yeah, the quantization axis is messy. The model variant we used is a 4-bit path with perf kernels, real nice token throughput but we saw subtle tokenization alignment issues causing alignment drift on structured outputs. Might be either the quantizer or preprocessing divergence.
[01:32] Leah: Also, our telemetry didn't capture the kv-cache mismatch well. We had traces for latency and for token generation count, but the prefix cache evictions weren't tagged with the model_variant in some of the older agents — artifact from the pre-2026 agent roll.
[01:47] Jonah: That was painful. During the spike we couldn't easily see which requests hit prefix versus full compute, so rollback had to be more conservative.
[01:55] Samir: Right— that's a big operating risk. If we can't slice by cache behavior, our SREs will always be in slow mode.
[02:05] Maya: Actionable then: telemetry tagging for prefix/cache/model_variant is priority. Jonah, Leah, you pair on a patch and we test on staging.
[02:12] Jonah: Yep, we can do a hotfix to the agent to add model_variant tags — there's a small perf cost but worth it.
[02:18] Maya: Good. Next — rollback criteria. In the dec run we used a hybrid threshold: 10% error rate uplift OR 20% latency P95 increase sustained for 3 minutes. That worked kinda but it created noise.
[02:34] Ari: I wanted to flag that thresholds need route-level calibration. The customer-facing assistant path and internal batch rerank path have wildly different tolerances. Aggregating at service level masked the kind of brittle regressions we saw.
[02:48] Elena: Can we get more fine-grained SLOs per route? We have tooling but someone needs to declare the SLOs.
[02:55] Maya: Ari, can you own per-route SLO declaration for the pilot?
[02:59] Ari: Yes — I'll draft a table with SLO, owners, and default rollback levels.
[03:05] Samir: Also a quick note: communicate rollback actions to the product execs. The last rollback surprised a few downstream teams.
[03:12] Rina: We had a follow-on ticket backlog spike because some consumer jobs retried. We need to include communication playbook.
[03:20] Maya: Add communication to the runbook: who to notify, and the template. Leah, can infra own the notification scaffolding? (like an automated page or slack channel ping)
[03:28] Leah: Yeah — we can do a page that triggers from ops runbook. Will need a small webhook endpoint to post structured payloads.
[03:35] Jonah: re observability, I want to mention sampling. During the event our distributed traces were sample-skewed and we lost the tail traces. We need adaptive sampling tied to error rate spikes.
[03:46] Carlos: We've got a prototype for adaptive sampling in the trace router, but it hasn't been rolled to prod. I'll prioritise a light version for the canary.
[03:54] Maya: Okay — Carlos, light adaptive sampling for canary by 2027-01-07.
[03:59] Carlos: noted.
[04:02] (murmur)
[04:10] [05:15] (speaker label confusion) Speaker 1: and then I think the other big learn was cost visibility, we didn't have a per-variant accounting for a week, so cost delta analysis was late.
[05:28] Leah: yeah cost was visible at pool level but not at model-variant level. We need token-level tagging in billing pipeline.
[05:36] Samir: Can the billing pipeline accept model_variant as a dimension?
[05:39] Carlos: It's not trivial but doable. It will add cardinality — we should compress model_variant into family+quantization fingerprint for rollups.
[05:50] Maya: Great. Next, on the product side — evaluation regressions. Rina, you mentioned a specific eval set which spiked hallucinations?
[05:58] Rina: The structured-qa eval (private prompt set) showed a 6 point BLEU-style drop in expected structured fields. It's a deterministic failing example cluster that we can use as a guardrail.
[06:10] Ari: Could we have pushed a smaller test subset to prod as a litmus before full flip?
[06:15] Maya: We should. Result: add preflight litmus test that runs against canonical set and fails the rollout if regressions exceed X. Who owns that?
[06:22] Rina: I'll own the litmus and keep it in the pipeline.
[06:25] Maya: Good.
[06:27] [07:00] Jonah: One operational nit — during the fast-fail we did a manual routing change that increased load on older pods and caused OOMs. The autoscaler didn't react because the OOMs looked like short-lived spikes. We need a safer way to flip traffic and smoother capacity reservation.
[07:18] Leah: We can add a safety cushion in the scheduler for canary traffic and a pre-warm step for older pools.
[07:25] Jonah: also add circuit breakers for mem pressure — auto-evict rather than fail hard.
[07:31] Carlos: For the runtime, we can lower max_batch size for older pods to avoid memory amplification when kv-cache misses occur.
[07:38] Maya: Okay, tactical items: pre-warm, mem-circuit breaker, batch-size adjust — Leah, Jonah, Carlos split these?
[07:46] Leah: I'll do pre-warm + scheduler flags.
[07:49] Jonah: I'll do mem-circuit breaker policy and charting.
[07:52] Carlos: I'll do batch-size tuning and add guardrail param in runtime.
[07:56] Maya: Great.
[08:00] [09:20] (overlap) Speaker 2: there's also the human process friction — the oncall rotation didn't have someone who owned the fast-fail flip. We need a clear role: flip-owner, rollback-owner, comms-owner.
[09:36] Samir: Agree. We'll make flip-owner the oncall first responder, rollback-owner is the SRE lead, comms-owner is product ops.
[09:45] Elena: Don't forget legal/compliance for certain customers — they require a 24 hour notice for changes to their inference path. We need a gating policy for regulated accounts.
[09:58] Maya: Good catch — adding a gating policy: for regulated accounts we require staged rollout with pre-approval. Ari, can you add account-level gating table?
[10:06] Ari: Yup.
[10:10] [11:30] Rina: One more procedural thing — the postmortem took too long to publish; part of that is ownership ambiguity. We should auto-create the PM draft and assign owners in the runbook.
[10:20] Maya: fine. We'll template the postmortem.
[10:23] Carlos: small technical note: the quantized kernels performed well on throughput but some math underflow in the int4 GEMM path caused occasional token dropouts under certain prompt shapes. Might need a hybrid kernel that uses FP16 when encountering structured tokens.
[10:40] Jonah: can we detect token shapes cheaply? Might be expensive.
[10:44] Carlos: cheap heuristics exist — prefix token flags, or content hashing; we'll prototype.
[10:49] Maya: For the canary we should avoid risky hybrid toggles; keep one dimension at a time. So either quantization OR cache eviction, not both. Agree?
[10:58] (short yeses)
[11:02] Samir: Yes. Keep variables orthogonal.
[11:05] Maya: Recap of owners — Jonah/Leah telemetry tagging; Carlos adaptive sampling + batch tuning; Ari per-route SLOs + gating; Rina litmus tests + postmortem template; Leah runbook notifications; Samir stake comms and exec notification flow. Next steps in the doc.
[11:22] [12:00] (crosstalk)
[11:30] Elena: ok timeline check — can we hit pilot canary january 10?
[11:34] Jonah: yes if tagging work is done this week and runbook done by 1/7.
[11:38] Leah: agreed.
[11:40] Maya: Any blockers?
[11:42] Rina: I'll need a small env to run the litmus; ops needs to provision it.
[11:46] Leah: Ops will provision by 2026-12-22.
[11:49] Maya: Great. Anyone object to the proposed communication plan?
[11:52] (silence)
[11:54] Maya: With no objections, we'll proceed. I'll send the meeting notes and owners and pin the runbook edits in #runbooks.
[11:59] Samir: One last ask — let's include a light cost SLO to avoid surprises; e.g., per-variant cost delta alert over 30% sustained for 24h.
[12:10] Carlos: ok, I'll add a metric and alert.
[12:15] Maya: Perfect. Thanks all — enjoy the holidays.
[12:20] (meeting ends)
